scope.description: Hand-researched deepening pass for English Expedition Base Set and five rows that expose the e-Card transition.

sources.title: Local English WoC release catalog: Expedition Base Set
Pokémon TCG API v2 set record: Expedition Base Set

claims.text: The local catalog and Pokémon TCG API model Expedition Base Set with a September 15, 2002 English release date; Bulbapedia also states the English expansion was released on September 15, 2002.
The local catalog and Pokémon TCG API both model 165 Expedition Base Set rows for set id ecard1.

Bulbapedia describes Expedition Base Set as the first main English expansion of the e-Card Series and says the Japanese counterpart was Base Expansion Pack, the first expansion of the Pokémon Card Game e-Card Era.

Bulbapedia says Expedition Base Set introduced Technical Machine cards, split Pokémon Power into Poké-Power and Poké-Body, and redesigned the card frame with enlarged left and bottom borders for Nintendo e-Reader Dot Code technology.
Bulbapedia says the e-Reader could show Pokédex data, play minigames or tunes, and activate hidden attacks, while hidden attacks were not legal for tournament play.

The local catalog's attention rows for Expedition include Mew, Mewtwo, Raichu, Tyranitar, Venusaur, Blastoise, Charizard, Dragonite, Feraligatr, Gengar, and the three Kanto final evolutions across holo and non-holo rows.
The local catalog's credited-artist clusters for Expedition are led by Atsuko Nishida, Hajime Kusajima, Kagemaru Himeno, Kyoko Umemoto, Tomokazu Komiya, and Keiji Kinebuchi.

Expedition matters because the card stops being only a printed game object and becomes an interface: it still carries chase monsters and artist memory, but the border itself now stores machine-readable contact with a Game Boy Advance accessory.

not_claiming: e-Reader strip readability from catalog data
steps: Confirm the set id ecard1 and row number before importing Expedition context.
Preserve holo, non-holo, and reverse-holo status separately; many chase Pokémon have more than one Expedition row.
If a buyer cares about the e-Reader feature, ask for clear images of the left and bottom Dot Code borders rather than assuming scanability from catalog identity.
Do not treat hidden e-Reader attacks as tournament-legal gameplay without an explicit legality source.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Expedition identification is row plus interface: the e-Reader border is part of the card's identity, but catalog data does not prove a seller's strip is readable.
special_identification_instructions.trigger: Identifying Expedition Base Set cards or comparing holo/non-holo e-Card rows.

narrative.human_title: When the border became a machine
narrative.why_it_matters: Expedition is a beautiful hinge. The old Wizards chase language is still there: Charizard, Blastoise, Mew, Tyranitar, Venusaur. But the card frame has changed its job. The fat left and bottom borders are not just design; they are an attempt to make cardboard speak to hardware. For a catalog about assembly, Expedition is where the object admits it wants to be read by more than human eyes.

sources.title: Pokémon TCG API v2 card record: Blastoise ecard1-4

claims.text: The local catalog and Pokémon TCG API identify Blastoise 4 as a Rare Holo Expedition Stage 2 Pokémon row illustrated by Kimiya Masago.
The Pokémon TCG API records Blastoise 4 with the Poké-Power Jet Stream and the attack Energy Cannon.
Bulbapedia says the Blastoise holo print has e-Reader card ID B-77 and the non-holo print has card ID B-77-#, with the species, height, and weight present on the holo print.
Blastoise 4 is an ideal Expedition specimen because the same character memory now depends on row, finish, Poké-Power text, and e-Reader strip context rather than name alone.

steps: Confirm row 4 rather than row 37 before applying holo-print context.
Check whether the seller's card is holo, non-holo, or reverse holo; do not assume from the name Blastoise.
Ask for clear left/bottom border images if e-Reader strip condition matters.
Keep Kimiya Masago credit as catalog metadata, not physical-card proof.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Expedition Blastoise needs finish and row clarity because the holo/non-holo e-Reader identities are close but not interchangeable.
special_identification_instructions.trigger: A buyer or seller references Expedition Blastoise.

narrative.human_title: The cannon turtle in machine-readable dress
narrative.why_it_matters: Expedition Blastoise still has the blunt old appeal of a Kanto final evolution. What changes is the wrapper: Poké-Power, e-Reader IDs, border codes, holo/non-holo identity. The card teaches an agent to look at the apparatus around the monster.

sources.title: Pokémon TCG API v2 card record: Charizard ecard1-6

claims.text: The local catalog and Pokémon TCG API identify Charizard 6 as a Rare Holo Expedition Stage 2 Pokémon row illustrated by Hiromichi Sugiyama.
The Pokémon TCG API records Charizard 6 with the Poké-Power Burning Energy and the attack Scorching Whirlwind.
The local catalog also contains Expedition Charizard rows 39 and 40, so Charizard 6 should not be treated as the only Expedition Charizard identity.

Charizard 6 keeps the familiar chase-monster gravity while Expedition changes the grammar around it: a Poké-Power, an e-Card frame, and a separate non-holo row mean the agent has to preserve row-level identity.

not_claiming: all Expedition Charizard rows are the same card
steps: Confirm whether the listing is row 6, 39, or 40 before importing art, attack, or value context.
For row 6, preserve Rare Holo status, Hiromichi Sugiyama credit, Burning Energy, and Scorching Whirlwind.
Ask for images of the row number and e-Reader borders if the seller only says Expedition Charizard.
Do not let Charizard's character gravity erase the row distinction.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Expedition Charizard is a row-identity trap: row 6, row 39, and row 40 carry different card contexts.
special_identification_instructions.trigger: A buyer or seller says Expedition Charizard without row number or image clarity.

narrative.human_title: The familiar fire with new machinery
narrative.why_it_matters: Charizard makes every set louder, but Expedition asks for more discipline than awe. Row 6 is not just 'the Expedition Charizard'; it is the holo Poké-Power version, sitting beside other Charizard rows in a machine-readable frame.

sources.title: Pokémon TCG API v2 card record: Charizard ecard1-39

claims.text: The local catalog and Pokémon TCG API identify Charizard 39 as a Rare Expedition Stage 2 Pokémon row illustrated by Atsuko Nishida.
The Pokémon TCG API records Charizard 39 with Tail Smash and Flamethrower rather than the Burning Energy / Scorching Whirlwind package on Charizard 6 and 40.
Bulbapedia says the English Charizard 39 print mistakenly says 'Put Charizard on the Basic Pokémon' instead of Stage 1 Pokémon.
Bulbapedia says Charizard 39 has two prints: the non-holo print has card ID A-12-#, while the holofoil print has card ID A-12.
Charizard 39 is the variant trap inside the chase: it is a Charizard, but its artist, attacks, error text, and e-Reader ID context differ from the other Expedition Charizard rows.

not_claiming: all English copies have identical visible condition
catalog error note proves a seller image
steps: Confirm row 39 and look for Tail Smash / Flamethrower before applying the documented error-text context.
Do not import Burning Energy / Scorching Whirlwind from Charizard 6 or 40 onto row 39.
Ask for a clear image of the evolution text area if the error matters to the buyer.
Keep the Atsuko Nishida credit separate from the Hiromichi Sugiyama Charizard rows.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Charizard 39 is not just another Expedition Charizard; its attack package, artist credit, and documented English evolution-text error need row-specific handling.
special_identification_instructions.trigger: A listing references Expedition Charizard 39, error text, or a non-holo Charizard without clear row evidence.

narrative.why_it_matters: This is the card an overconfident agent would flatten. It says Charizard, but the real story is in the row: Atsuko Nishida, Tail Smash, Flamethrower, e-Reader ID, and a famous little evolution-text mistake. The name is loud; the evidence is quiet.

sources.title: Pokémon TCG API v2 card record: Mew ecard1-19

claims.text: The local catalog and Pokémon TCG API identify Mew 19 as a Rare Holo Expedition Basic Pokémon row illustrated by Hajime Kusajima.
The Pokémon TCG API records Mew 19 with the attack Super Psywave.
Bulbapedia says the holofoil Expedition Mew print has card ID B-85, while the non-holo Expedition print and P Promotional print have card ID B-85-#.

Bulbapedia says the non-holo Expedition Mew print and P Promotional print include short-strip information about Pokédex data, a brief card summary, and long-strip content; the species, height, and weight are present on the holofoil Expedition print.
Mew 19 turns Expedition's interface story into a chase-card problem: the mythic Pokémon is still the draw, but the holo/non-holo/P Promo e-Reader data distinctions become part of what the card is.

not_claiming: Mew 19, Mew 55, and P Promotional Mew are interchangeable
steps: Confirm whether the card is Expedition row 19, Expedition row 55, or a P Promotional print before using the e-Reader ID context.
Preserve holofoil status for row 19 and do not assume it from the name Mew.
Ask for clear strip and row-number images if the buyer cares about e-Reader data or print identity.
Treat long-strip/hidden-content references as catalog context, not proof that a seller's physical card scans.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Expedition Mew requires row, finish, and e-Reader data context; the name alone is much too broad.
special_identification_instructions.trigger: A buyer or seller says Expedition Mew, Mew 19, Mew 55, or P Promotional Mew.

narrative.why_it_matters: Mew is already a perfect collector creature: rare, soft, a little impossible. Expedition adds another layer of impossibility by making the card carry machine-readable data. The wonder is no longer only in the art window; it is in the strip beside it.

sources.title: Pokemon TCG API v2 card record: Mewtwo ecard1-20

claims.text: The local catalog and Pokemon TCG API identify Mewtwo as English Expedition Base Set row ecard1-20 / printed number 20.
The local catalog and Pokemon TCG API classify Mewtwo ecard1-20 as a Rare Holo Pokemon card.
The local catalog and Pokemon TCG API credit Kimiya Masago as the illustrator for Mewtwo ecard1-20.
The Pokemon TCG API payload models Mewtwo ecard1-20 as a Psychic Basic Pokemon with HP 70, Psychic weakness, retreat cost 2, and the attacks Hypnosis and Psychic.

Mewtwo ecard1-20 matters because Expedition moves the laboratory legend into the e-Reader interface era: the card is still a holo chase, but the expanded border, row identity, and reverse-holo possibility make the physical edge part of the evidence story.

Agents should distinguish Mewtwo ecard1-20 from Base Set Mewtwo, Base Set 2 Mewtwo, Legendary Collection Mewtwo, Japanese Expansion Pack / No Rarity Mewtwo, P Promotional Mewtwo 046/P, and later Mewtwo ex/GX/V memory; the Expedition row number, set id ecard1, Rare Holo status, Kimiya Masago credit, Hypnosis/Psychic text, and e-Reader border condition are load-bearing.

steps: Confirm the row as Expedition Base Set / ecard1 printed number 20 before using this dossier.
Check the card is the Rare Holo Mewtwo with Kimiya Masago credit, Hypnosis, Psychic, HP 70, Psychic weakness, and retreat cost 2.
Preserve Expedition's e-Reader frame as identity context, but do not infer that a seller's physical card scans or has readable Dot Code borders.
Keep holofoil and reverse-holo status separate; ask for clear front/angle images if finish matters.
Separate this row from Base Set Mewtwo, Base Set 2 Mewtwo, Legendary Collection Mewtwo, Japanese Expansion Pack / No Rarity Mewtwo, P Promotional Mewtwo 046/P, and later Mewtwo ex/GX/V memories.
Treat price, condition, authenticity, finish, e-Reader readability, and slab status as separately sourced transaction claims; catalog identity only makes the row legible.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Mewtwo ecard1-20 is the Expedition Base Set Rare Holo row. Preserve set id, row number, finish, and e-Reader-border evidence before comparing to other Mewtwo prints.
special_identification_instructions.trigger: A buyer or seller says Expedition Mewtwo, e-Reader Mewtwo, Mewtwo 20, ecard1-20, reverse-holo Mewtwo, or Kimiya Masago Mewtwo.

card_highlights.collector_texture_note: Expedition Mewtwo is the lab legend moving through the e-Reader frame: Masago art, holo finish, Hypnosis/Psychic text, and a border that asks to be read as interface.

narrative.human_title: Mewtwo 20: the lab myth at the edge of the scanner
narrative.why_it_matters: Expedition Mewtwo feels like the character crossing a threshold. Base Mewtwo is the launch binder's unease; P Promo Mewtwo is a rail-station contact object; Expedition Mewtwo is the same myth pressed into a card frame that wants a machine to read it. Kimiya Masago's credit, Hypnosis, Psychic, holo finish, and the e-Reader border all matter because the card is no longer only image and text. It is an interface object. For an agent, that means ecard1-20 first, finish and strip evidence second, condition and authenticity only after seller proof.

sources.title: Pokémon TCG API v2 card record: Tyranitar ecard1-29

claims.text: The local catalog and Pokémon TCG API identify Tyranitar 29 as a Rare Holo Expedition Stage 2 Darkness Pokémon row illustrated by Kimiya Masago.
The Pokémon TCG API records Tyranitar 29 with the Poké-Body Dark Aura and the attack Stamp.
Bulbapedia says Tyranitar 29 was included as holofoil and non-holofoil in Expedition and that a reverse-holo jumbo print was released as a box topper in English booster boxes.
Bulbapedia says the holofoil and box-topper Tyranitar prints have card ID B-95, while the non-holo print has card ID B-95-#.
Tyranitar 29 is Expedition's heavy Johto presence: the card brings Darkness typing, Poké-Body vocabulary, and a box-topper branch into one row family.

not_claiming: standard-size holo and jumbo box topper are interchangeable
steps: Confirm whether the card is standard-size row 29, standard-size row 66, or the reverse-holo jumbo box topper.
Preserve Dark Aura / Stamp context for the Tyranitar 29 family.
Ask for scale or surrounding-object evidence if a seller image could be jumbo or standard-size.
Do not treat e-Reader card ID B-95 alone as enough to distinguish standard holo from box topper without size/format evidence.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Expedition Tyranitar has standard and box-topper branches; size, row, finish, and e-Reader ID all matter.
special_identification_instructions.trigger: A listing references Expedition Tyranitar, a box topper, jumbo print, or card ID B-95.

narrative.human_title: The mountain-breaker gets a second format
narrative.why_it_matters: Tyranitar is already built like a warning sign. Expedition makes that warning multi-format: holo, non-holo, and jumbo box topper orbit the same heavy Johto identity. For an agent, the fun is also the danger: one monster, several physical meanings.
